title: Shanghai Jiao Tong University medical school vows thorough probe into clinical case following reports of death of 6-year-old girl after gene-editing trial - Global Times
summary: Shanghai Jiao Tong University Medical School has pledged a thorough investigation after reports that a 6-year-old girl died following participation in a gene-editing clinical trial. The statement promises cooperation with regulators and a review of clinical procedures, but details remain sparse and unverified. The case has prompted renewed calls for transparency and regulatory oversight of gene-editing research involving children in China.
content:
Shanghai Jiao Tong University Medical School on Thursday said it would conduct a thorough probe into a clinical case after reports emerged that a 6-year-old girl died following participation in a gene-editing trial, according to a Global Times report.

The medical school said it would cooperate with relevant authorities and review the clinical procedures, informed consent processes and oversight associated with the case. The university did not release identifying details about the child or the clinical project in its initial statement, and it described the inquiry as ongoing.

Media reports and social media posts have circulated details and allegations, but the university statement cautioned that information available publicly remains incomplete and unverified. Officials said they would disclose findings when appropriate and urged the public to await results of the formal investigation.

Separately, Chinese authorities have continued to act on a range of research and public-health concerns. The report noted that China's National Health Commission announced disciplinary measures following a public misconduct case, and other academic institutions have launched probes into research and school incidents.

For instance, Lanzhou University has initiated an investigation into a research paper published by a faculty member in an international academic journal, and local reports said 94 students at the Puning Huamei experimental school in Lufeng, Guangdong Province, developed illness tied to an incident at the primary department. These items were cited alongside the medical-school statement in the same news coverage.

The alleged death of a child after a gene-editing trial highlights broader ethical and safety concerns about editing human genes, particularly in minors. Observers and bioethicists have repeatedly called for strict oversight, clear consent procedures, independent safety monitoring and transparency in clinical research involving new genetic technologies.

Authorities and the university said they would provide updates as the inquiry progresses. In the meantime, calls for a transparent, accountable investigation have intensified among academics, clinicians and the public, who seek clarity on how the trial was conducted and whether proper safeguards were in place.
